title: capwall capabilities.json
description: Per-package capability policy for the capwall runtime firewall. Authoritative field docs: docs/policy-format.md. Keep in sync with packages/policy-schema/src/index.ts.

mode.description: Enforcement mode this policy declares, used by `capwall run` and by a bare @capwall/core/preload. An explicit CAPWALL_MODE (which `capwall observe` / `capwall enforce` / `capwall diff` set) always wins. Omitted = no declared mode: a modeless invocation stays inert.

default.description: Applied to any package with no explicit entry in `packages`. Recommended: grant nothing (deny-by-default).

packages.description: Map of package name to its capability grant.

packagePolicy.description: Per-package capability grant. Every field optional; omitted = not granted.

hosts.description: Allowed hosts: an exact hostname, the single literal "*" (any host), or a wildcard pattern — "*.internal" (exactly one label) or "**.internal" (one or more). A wildcard never crosses a dot and never matches an IP literal; IP addresses (IPv6 unbracketed) must be listed exactly. Matching lowercases ASCII A-Z only; no IDNA conversion, so list the punycode form Node dials. Malformed patterns are rejected at load time. See docs/policy-format.md § net.

ipc.description: Unix-domain sockets and Windows named pipes this package may connect to (#72). Without it, IPC is denied.

paths.description: Socket-path globs, matched by the same matcher fs grants use. Relative patterns resolve against the project root; <tmp>/<home> expand against the loading machine; a Windows named pipe may be written \\.\pipe\NAME or //./pipe/NAME. The legacy net: {hosts: ["<ipc>"], ports: [0]} grant still means EVERY socket and pipe.

child_process.description: Gate: may this package spawn subprocesses? (gating, not confinement)

worker_threads.description: Gate: may this package start worker threads?

env.description: Allowlist of process.env keys this package may read. ["*"] allows all.

vm.description: Gate: may this package use node:vm?

native.description: Gate: may this package load a native (.node) addon? Boolean, not a path list, because addon paths are platform/arch/ABI-specific build artifacts and would not reproduce across machines. Gating only — once an addon loads, capwall cannot confine it.

compile.description: Gate: may this package call Module.prototype._compile directly with a filename outside its own package? IDENTITY-GRANTING — V8 reports the chosen filename on every resulting stack frame, so a package with this grant can run code as any principal in the policy, including <app>. Needed only by require.extensions transform hooks (ts-node, @babel/register, pirates, require-in-the-middle). Granting it is granting every other grant in this file.
